items.title: Steve Allen interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 15, 1999
items.q: One of my hit songs... it’s called “Pretend You Don’t See My Heart.” It was a big hit by Jerry Vale

ctx.x: If you sit and write a tune that’s really meant to be an instrumental, such as the thing you did with Benny Goodman or something like that, is it sometimes a little chore to think of a title to put on it?

That also is a marvelous question, that’s what you do for a living, you ask marvelous questions. I jump back to, I don’t know about 40 years ago, I once got intrigued by that question, and I wrote to about 20 band leaders, including Benny. This was long before I’d met him. He had some instrumentals, one was called “Benji’s Bauble,” and another one with the name of one of his daughters. Now I didn’t know that those were named after two of children until he wrote back and said Dear Steve, in answer to your…
Let me play a little excerpt, one of your many songs, and we were talking about some of your jazz work.
